ukberi-tibyan:10-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ (١٠) فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَالنَّخْلُ ذَاتُ الْأَكْمَامِ (١١))
His saying (لِلْأَنَامِ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to وَضَعَهَا.
It is also said: it is attached to what follows it, i.e. "for mankind «فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ»", so it is either the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), or an explanation (tabyīn).

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْحَبُّ ذُو الْعَصْفِ وَالرَّيْحَانُ (١٢))
His saying (وَالْحَبُّ) is read in the nominative, conjoined to «النَّخْلِ», and (وَالرَّيْحَانُ) likewise. It is also read in the accusative, i.e. "and He created الْحَبَّ ذَا الْعَصْفِ, and He created الرَّيْحَانَ".
It is also read الرَّيْحَانِ, in the genitive, conjoined to الْعَصْفِ.

ukberi-tibyan:14-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ صَلْصَالٍ كَالْفَخَّارِ (١٤) وَخَلَقَ الْجَانَّ مِنْ مَارِجٍ مِنْ نَارٍ (١٥))
His saying (كَالْفَخَّارِ): it is a naʿt (adjective) of صَلْصَالٍ. And (مِنْ نَارٍ) is a naʿt of مَارِجٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:17-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ الْمَغْرِبَيْنِ (١٧) فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ (١٨) مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ (١٩) بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ لَا يَبْغِيَانِ (٢٠))
His saying (رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ): i.e. "He is the Lord". It is also said: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is «مَرَجَ».
And (يَلْتَقِيَانِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And (بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يَلْتَقِيَانِ».
And (لَا يَبْغِيَانِ) is also a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ (٢٢))
His saying (يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا): they said: the implied meaning is "from one of the two":
«[Translator's note: the source text ends here with a colon; nothing follows in the edition used.]»

ukberi-tibyan:24-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَهُ الْجَوَارِ الْمُنْشَآتُ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلَامِ (٢٤) فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ (٢٥) كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ (٢٦))
His saying (الْمُنْشَآتُ): with fatḥa on the shīn, and this is the proper way. (فِي الْبَحْرِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it.
It is also read with kasra on it, i.e. "they bring about (tunshiʾu) the voyage", and this is figurative.
And (كَالْأَعْلَامِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «الْمُنْشَآتُ». The hāʾ in «عَلَيْهَا» refers to the earth, and its mention has preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَبْقَى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ (٢٧))
His saying (ذُو الْجَلَالِ): in the nominative it is a naʿt (adjective) of الْوَجْه; and in the genitive [ذِي] it is a naʿt of the genitive noun [رَبِّكَ].

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَسْأَلُهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ (٢٩))
His saying (كُلَّ يَوْمٍ): it is an adverb (ẓarf) for what is indicated by «هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ», i.e. "He turns affairs about every day".

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ الثَّقَلَانِ (٣١))
His saying (سَنَفْرُغُ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the rāʾ; it has also been read with fatḥa on it because of the guttural letter, and its past tense is فَرَغَ with fatḥa on the rāʾ.
فَرِغَ with kasra on the rāʾ has also been heard for it, so it takes fatḥa in the imperfect, like نَصِبَ يَنْصَبُ.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَنْفُذُوا مِنْ أَقْطَارِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانْفُذُوا لَا تَنْفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلْطَانٍ (٣٣))
His saying (لَا تَنْفُذُونَ): لَا is negating, in the sense of «مَا».

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُمَا شُوَاظٌ مِنْ نَارٍ وَنُحَاسٌ فَلَا تَنْتَصِرَانِ (٣٥))
And (شُوَاظٌ) with ḍamma and with kasra are two dialectal forms, and it has been read with both. And (مِنْ نَارٍ) is an adjective (ṣifa), or attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb.
(وَنُحَاسٌ) in the nominative is conjoined to شُوَاظٍ, and in the genitive it is conjoined to نَارٍ; the nominative is stronger in meaning, because النُّحَاسُ is smoke, and that is the شُوَاظُ (flame) of the fire.

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِذَا انْشَقَّتِ السَّمَاءُ فَكَانَتْ وَرْدَةً كَالدِّهَانِ (٣٧))
And (الدِّهَانُ) is the plural of دُهْنٍ (oil); it is also said: it is a singular, meaning a leather mat (النِّطْعُ).

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لَا يُسْأَلُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إِنْسٌ وَلَا جَانٌّ (٣٩))
(جَانٌّ) is the fāʿil (agent) [i.e. the deputy agent of the passive verb].
It is also read with a hamza [جَأْنٌّ], because the alif was given a vowel and so changed into a hamza; this was mentioned in al-Fātiḥa.
«[Translator's note: the source calls جَانٌّ a fāʿil although يُسْأَلُ is passive; the bracketed clarification is added.]»

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍ (٤٤))
His saying (يَطُوفُونَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْمُجْرِمِينَ», and it may be resumptive.
And (آنٍ) is an active participle (fāʿil-pattern), like قَاضٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَوَاتَا أَفْنَانٍ (٤٨))
His saying (ذَوَاتَا): the alif before the tāʾ is a replacement for a yāʾ; it is also said: for a wāw. It is an adjective (ṣifa) of جَنَّتَانِ, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). And الْأَفْنَانُ is the plural of فَنَنٍ, which is a branch.

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَى فُرُشٍ بَطَائِنُهَا مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ وَجَنَى الْجَنَّتَيْنِ دَانٍ (٥٤))
His saying (مُتَّكِئِينَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «خَافَ», and what governs it is the adverbial expression (al-ẓarf).
His saying (مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ): the origin of the word is a verb on the pattern اسْتَفْعَلَ; when it was used as a name, its hamza was made a disjunctive hamza (hamzat qaṭʿ). It is also said: it is foreign (aʿjamī).
It has also been read with the hamza dropped and kasra on the nūn. This is a mistake, because that does not occur in nouns, but only in maṣdars and verbs.

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فِيهِنَّ قَاصِرَاتُ الطَّرْفِ لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إِنْسٌ قَبْلَهُمْ وَلَا جَانٌّ (٥٦))
His saying (فِيهِنَّ): the pronoun may refer to the dwellings of the two gardens, or to the couches (الْفُرُش), i.e. "upon them". And الطَّرْف was made singular because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).
And (لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ) is a description of قَاصِرَاتِ, because the annexation is not pure (ghayr maḥḍa); and likewise «كَأَنَّهُنَّ الْيَاقُوتُ».
«[Translator's note: the source has الظَّرْفُ ("the adverb") where the context requires الطَّرْفُ ("the glance"); it is translated here as الطَّرْف.]»

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَلْ جَزَاءُ الْإِحْسَانِ إِلَّا الْإِحْسَانُ (٦٠))
And (الْإِحْسَانِ) [i.e. the second الْإِحْسَانُ] is the khabar (predicate) of جَزَاءُ, and إِلَّا entered in accordance with the meaning [the interrogative having the sense of negation].
«[Translator's note: the bracketed clarifications are added.]»

ukberi-tibyan:70-72.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فِيهِنَّ خَيْرَاتٌ حِسَانٌ (٧٠) فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ (٧١) حُورٌ مَقْصُورَاتٌ فِي الْخِيَامِ (٧٢))
His saying (خَيْرَاتٌ): it is the plural of خَيْرَةٍ; one says: امْرَأَةٌ خَيْرَةٌ (a good woman). It has also been read with a doubled yāʾ. And (حُورٌ) is a badal (substitute) from «خَيْرَاتٌ». It is also said: the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "in them are حُورٌ".

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَى رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ وَعَبْقَرِيٍّ حِسَانٍ (٧٦))
And (مُتَّكِئِينَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) is omitted, indicated by the pronoun in «قَبْلَهُمْ».
And (رَفْرَفٍ) has a plural meaning; that is why it is described by «خُضْرٍ». It has also been read رَفْرَافٍ, and likewise «عَبْقَرِيٍّ».

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تَبَارَكَ اسْمُ رَبِّكَ ذِي الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ (٧٨))
And (ذِي الْجَلَالِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of رَبِّكَ; this is stronger than the nominative, because the name (al-ism) is not so described. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الرَّحْمَنُ (١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الرَّحْمَنُ): some held that it is (by itself) a verse; on this view the implied wording is "Allah is the Most Merciful" (اللَّهُ الرَّحْمَنُ), so that the speech is complete. According to the view of the others, «الرَّحْمَنُ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what follows it is the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:3-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ (٣) عَلَّمَهُ الْبَيَانَ (٤)).
And (خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ) is resumptive, and likewise «عَلَّمَهُ». It may also be an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, circumstantial) from الْإِنْسَان, with «قَدْ» intended with it.

ukberi-tibyan:5-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ (٥) وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ (٦) وَالسَّمَاءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِحُسْبَانٍ), i.e. "they run by a reckoning". (وَالسَّمَاءَ) in the accusative by an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned; this is preferable to the nominative because it is conjoined to a noun that a verb has governed, namely the pronoun in «يَسْجُدَانِ»; or it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الْإِنْسَانَ».

ukberi-tibyan:8-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا فِي الْمِيزَانِ (٨) وَأَقِيمُوا الْوَزْنَ بِالْقِسْطِ وَلَا تُخْسِرُوا الْمِيزَانَ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ لَا تَطْغَوْا), i.e. "so that you do not transgress" (لِئَلَّا تَطْغَوْا).
It is also said that «لَا» is for prohibition, and أَنْ means "that is" (أَيْ, explicative), the verb of saying being implied. And (تُخْسِرُوا) with ḍamma on the tāʾ, i.e. "and do not diminish what is weighed".
It is also said that the implied wording is "in the balance". It is also read with fatḥa on the sīn and the tāʾ (تَخْسَرُوا), its past tense being خَسِرَ; the first is sounder.
